mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic output and capacity utilization, which typically supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases both interest rates and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 6-month moving minimum, combined with a concurrent drop in personal income (PAYEMS), signals a collapse in residential investment and consumer purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 6-month minimum AND PAYEMS declines month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls below its 6-month minimum and PAYEMS declines month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer demand and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An above-consensus rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) coupled with a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) indicates a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises above consensus AND GDPC1 declines month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises above consensus and GDPC1 declines month-over-month.
